sops.title: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH, SAFETY AND EMPLOYEE WELLBEING GUIDELINES

blocks.text:
To establish preventive measures for protecting employees from occupational health risks and promoting a safe and supportive workplace. This SOP provides guidelines for ergonomic risk management, prevention of repetitive strain injuries, workplace stress and psychological wellbeing, hazardous substance exposure control, and occupational noise exposure.

The SOP aims to minimize occupational health risks through appropriate risk identification, preventive controls, employee awareness, monitoring, and continual improvement.

This SOP applies to all employees, contract personnel, trainees, and other persons working within the organization's operational areas, offices, laboratories, warehouses, maintenance areas, and other applicable workplaces.

responsibilities: Identification and assessment of occupational health risks, implementation of preventive controls, monitoring, training, and compliance oversight.
Coordination of employee wellbeing initiatives, communication channels, and applicable employee support measures.
Support for occupational health assessments, medical evaluation, health surveillance, and appropriate follow-up, where applicable.
Implementation of occupational health controls within their respective work areas and ensuring employee adherence to safe work practices.
Maintenance of equipment, engineering controls, ventilation systems, noise-control systems, and other occupational health-related infrastructure.
Follow established safe work practices, use required PPE, participate in training and monitoring activities, and report occupational health concerns or unsafe conditions.
Identification of task-level risks, implementation of controls, employee communication, and follow-up of identified corrective actions.

rows.role: Factory Medical Officer / Occupational Health Function, where applicable
Senior Management for strategic planning and resource allocation

steps.heading: Ergonomics and Prevention of Repetitive Strain Injuries

body.text:
Identify work activities involving repetitive movements, prolonged static postures, awkward postures, forceful exertion, frequent lifting or other activities that may contribute to musculoskeletal discomfort or repetitive strain injuries.
Conduct ergonomic risk assessments for relevant workstations, tasks and work processes.
Consider factors such as task frequency, duration, posture, force, reach, workstation arrangement and available recovery periods when assessing ergonomic risks.
Identify employees or work groups exposed to significant ergonomic risks and prioritize appropriate preventive measures.

Optimize workstations, tools, equipment and work layouts to reduce awkward postures, excessive reaching, unnecessary force and repetitive movements.
Where technically feasible, provide suitable mechanical aids, adjustable workstations, appropriate tools or other engineering solutions to reduce ergonomic strain.
Review task design and work methods to identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary repetition and excessive physical effort.
Ensure that ergonomic improvements do not compromise process safety, product quality or operational requirements.

steps.heading: Repetitive Task and Manual Handling Controls

body.text:
Evaluate repetitive tasks and manual handling activities and implement suitable controls based on the identified risk.
Use appropriate handling aids or equipment where manual handling presents a significant ergonomic risk.
Where applicable, organize work activities to reduce prolonged exposure to repetitive or physically demanding tasks.
Provide employees with appropriate guidance on safe posture, task execution and manual handling practices.

Provide awareness or training to employees performing tasks with identified ergonomic risks.
Encourage employees to report early signs of musculoskeletal discomfort, repetitive strain or other work-related ergonomic concerns to their supervisor, Safety/EHS or Occupational Health function.
Reported ergonomic concerns shall be evaluated and appropriate corrective or preventive actions shall be identified.
Where required, work activities or workstation arrangements shall be reviewed following reported ergonomic concerns.

Identify workplace factors that may contribute to excessive work-related stress, including excessive workload, prolonged working hours, work organization, inadequate communication, interpersonal concerns or other relevant workplace factors.
Where appropriate, assess identified psychosocial risks as part of workplace risk assessments or employee wellbeing reviews.
Maintain appropriate confidentiality when handling individual employee wellbeing concerns.
Employees shall be provided with appropriate channels to raise workplace concerns without fear of retaliation.

Promote a work environment that supports respectful communication, reasonable work organization and appropriate employee support.
Where significant work-related stress risks are identified, evaluate appropriate organizational or work-practice improvements.
Encourage supervisors and managers to identify workload, work-organization or workplace issues that may adversely affect employee wellbeing.
Promote awareness of available employee support resources and encourage employees to seek assistance when required.

Identify work activities, processes and job roles where employees may be exposed to hazardous chemicals, substances, vapours, gases, dusts or other hazardous materials.
Evaluate potential exposure routes, including inhalation, skin contact, eye contact or accidental ingestion, as applicable to the substance and task.
Consider the hazardous properties of substances, quantity handled, duration/frequency of exposure, process conditions and existing controls when assessing exposure risks.
Use applicable SDS/MSDS and chemical hazard information when evaluating occupational exposure risks.

Provide appropriate PPE based on the identified hazardous-substance exposure risk and applicable SDS/assessment requirements.
Employees shall use, maintain and store assigned PPE in accordance with established requirements.
Employees handling hazardous substances shall follow applicable safe work procedures, SDS instructions and emergency-response requirements.
Damaged or unsuitable PPE shall be replaced as required.

Where required based on risk assessment, applicable regulatory requirements or occupational-health considerations, conduct workplace exposure monitoring for relevant hazardous substances.
Where applicable, establish appropriate occupational health or medical surveillance for employees with identified exposure risks.

Provide employees with information and training on hazardous-substance hazards, exposure routes, safe handling practices, PPE requirements, emergency measures and applicable SDS information.
Provide additional training when significant changes are made to chemicals, processes, equipment or exposure-control measures.
Employees shall be informed of applicable workplace controls and the importance of reporting leaks, spills, unusual exposures or unsafe conditions.

Identify work areas, equipment and activities where employees may be exposed to elevated occupational noise levels.
Consider equipment such as rotating machinery, compressors, pumps, boilers, production equipment and other relevant noise-generating sources during assessment.
Identify employees or work groups who may require additional noise exposure controls based on workplace assessment.
Maintain identification of designated high-noise areas, where applicable.

Conduct workplace noise measurements in relevant employee work areas using suitable and calibrated noise-measuring equipment.
Conduct periodic noise monitoring based on identified risks and applicable requirements.

Prioritize engineering controls to reduce occupational noise at the source, including equipment enclosure, acoustic treatment, muffling, isolation, vibration control or equipment maintenance, where technically feasible.
Maintain noise-generating equipment in suitable operating condition to minimize unnecessary noise generation.
Where engineering controls alone are insufficient, implement appropriate administrative or work-practice controls to reduce employee exposure duration.
Restrict access to designated high-noise areas where appropriate and communicate applicable requirements to employees and contractors.

Provide suitable hearing protection to employees working in areas where such protection is required based on the occupational noise assessment.
Provide employees with information on occupational noise hazards, hearing-protection requirements and appropriate use and maintenance of hearing protection.
Ensure employees understand applicable requirements for designated high-noise areas.
Replace damaged or unsuitable hearing-protection equipment as required.

steps.heading: Emergency Response for Occupational Health Incidents

body.text:
Maintain appropriate emergency arrangements for incidents involving hazardous-substance exposure, significant chemical releases, acute occupational health events or other workplace emergencies.
Provide appropriate emergency response equipment, PPE, first-aid facilities and other resources based on identified workplace risks.
Employees shall immediately report occupational exposure incidents, significant injuries, chemical exposure events or other occupational health emergencies to the concerned supervisor and Safety/EHS function.
Provide appropriate first aid and medical assistance based on the nature of the incident.
For hazardous-substance exposure, follow the applicable SDS/MSDS emergency and first-aid instructions.
Investigate significant occupational health incidents to identify root causes and corrective/preventive actions.
Maintain applicable emergency and incident records in accordance with the Incident Reporting and Investigation procedure.

blocks.text:
Identify opportunities to improve engineering controls, work practices, workplace arrangements and employee support measures.
Update risk assessments and control measures following significant process, equipment, chemical or workplace changes.
Review the effectiveness of implemented occupational health controls and initiate further improvements where required.
Update this SOP based on assessment findings, applicable regulatory requirements, technological developments and identified occupational health risks.

To identify areas of improvement and ensure actions are implemented with regard to emergency preparedness, response to incidents/accidents, and managing information security breaches to prevent further damage and reassure affected parties.
This procedure applies to all incidents, accidents, and information security breaches taking place at the TIL Ekalbara site and Registered Office.

responsibilities: Incident and security breach reporting.
Compliance with corrective actions.
Incident investigation.
Investigating and responding to information security breaches.

body.text: Incident includes work-related injuries, occupational illness, property damage, leakage, spillage, fire, near-miss events, and information security breaches such as unauthorized data access, phishing, malware attacks, and data leaks.

Near-miss, first-aid, non-reportable & reportable.

An incident causing bodily injury that allows the affected person to resume duty within 48 hours.

body.text:
Report incidents/accidents immediately to the safety department.
Fill the prescribed Incident/Accident Report Form (TIL-EKB-SFT-FF-04) for physical incidents and the Information Security Incident Report Form (TIL-EKB-IT-FF-01) for security breaches.
Submit reports to respective departments for verification and action.
Medical Officer and Safety Officer to document and evaluate the incident, suggesting corrective actions.

Report events such as fires, chemical spills, or significant cybersecurity breaches using the relevant forms (TIL-EKB-SFT-FF-05 or TIL-EKB-IT-FF-01).
Involve relevant personnel, including safety officers, IT teams, and section heads, to document and mitigate the issue.

Witnesses of near-misses must document them using the Near-miss Form (TIL-EKB-SFT-FF-13).
Report to the safety or IT department (for cybersecurity near-misses) within 24 hours.

Employees must immediately report suspected breaches, phishing attempts, or system anomalies to the IT Helpdesk.
The Information Security Officer will log the incident, assess the breach's scope, and initiate an investigation.

Investigate all incidents and breaches within 24 hours of occurrence.
Identify root causes and corrective actions.
Track corrective actions until completed.
Review trends, identify gaps, and develop improvement plans.

Conduct a thorough investigation by visiting the site (or analyzing system logs in case of breaches).
Interview affected individuals, witnesses, supervisors, or IT personnel.
Document findings in the relevant Incident Investigation Report (TIL-EKB-SFT-FF-14 or TIL-EKB-IT-FF-02).

Share incident details and corrective actions with concerned personnel, safety committees, or IT governance teams.
Include incidents in monthly safety and IT security meetings.
Revise related policies, HIRA, or work instructions based on findings.

Collaborate with the IT team to mitigate risks and recover data.
Communicate transparently with affected stakeholders about the breach and measures taken.

blocks.text: To define and implement effective strategies, technologies, and operational practices aimed at conserving water resources. This SOP focuses on water recycling, reuse, advanced cooling systems, groundwater protection, water-risk assessment and the integration of sustainable water management solutions across company operations.
This document applies to all processes and activities undertaken by the organization to reduce water consumption, maximize reuse, and prevent water resource contamination at all operational sites.

responsibilities: Implementation and monitoring of technologies and practices.
Ensuring adherence to legal and sustainability standards.
Regular inspection and maintenance of water conservation systems.
Supervision of daily operations to ensure compliance.
Strategic decision-making and resource allocation.

body.text:
Identify water sources for reclamation such as process water, wastewater.
Implement advanced water treatment technologies (e.g., membrane filtration, reverse osmosis, UV disinfection) to reclaim water.
Develop and maintain closed-loop water systems for internal reuse in production, cooling, and landscape irrigation.
Integrate water recycling systems with ECMs to enhance energy efficiency in water treatment and distribution.
Where technically and operationally feasible, identify additional opportunities for recycling and reuse of treated water to reduce freshwater consumption.
Evaluate suitable treated-water streams for reuse in utilities, cooling systems, gardening, or other approved non-potable applications, subject to applicable quality requirements

blocks.text:
Maintain technology installation records (e.g., water treatment units).
Regularly update work instructions for water recycling procedures.
Include data on reclaimed and reused water in the Annual Report or Sustainability Report.
Maintain records of water recycling and reuse activities, including available quantity/volume data and relevant treatment or water-quality records.

narrative.text:
Conduct regular assessments of treated water quality to ensure compliance with safety standards.
Implement continuous monitoring systems for critical water reuse operations.
Periodically review the performance of water recycling and reuse systems and identify opportunities for further improvement.

sections.title: Cooling Tower Operation and Water Efficiency

steps.heading: Cooling Tower Operation and Water Efficiency

body.text:
Operate cooling towers to optimize water consumption and minimize avoidable water losses.
Use RO-treated water as cooling tower make-up water, where technically and operationally appropriate.
Maintain appropriate cooling tower operating conditions, including monitoring of water quality and cycles of concentration (CoC), to minimize unnecessary blowdown.
Monitor cooling tower evaporation, blowdown, leakage, and other significant water losses.
Integrate waste heat recovery systems as part of ECMs to reduce cooling demands and associated water usage.
Identify opportunities for further reduction, recycling, or reuse of cooling tower water through water audits and periodic operational reviews.
Conduct routine inspection and maintenance of cooling towers to maintain efficient operation and prevent water losses.

blocks.text:
Maintain installation and maintenance records for cooling systems.
Develop SOPs for the operation and maintenance of water-efficient cooling equipment.
Include water consumption data for cooling purposes in the Annual Report.
Maintain records of cooling tower make-up water consumption and blowdown, where applicable.
Maintain cooling tower operation, inspection, maintenance, and water-quality monitoring records.
Maintain relevant cooling tower water-quality, CoC, inspection, and maintenance records.
Document water-efficiency measures implemented for cooling tower operations and available evidence of resulting water savings.

sections.title: Cooling Tower Monitoring and Performance Review

narrative.text:
Conduct routine maintenance of cooling systems to ensure efficiency.
Monitor and document water usage reduction achieved through adopted technologies.
Periodically review cooling tower water-use trends and identify opportunities for further water conservation.
Track measurable improvements resulting from cooling tower water-efficiency measures, where data is available.
Include significant cooling-water conservation initiatives in periodic environmental and sustainability performance reviews.

body.text:
Implement groundwater monitoring programs to detect potential pollutants, including heavy metals, nitrates, and organic compounds.
Establish control measures, such as:
Sealing potential contamination sources.
Designing and maintaining leak-proof chemical storage systems.
Treating industrial effluents to meet discharge standards before release.
Incorporate energy-efficient pumping and monitoring systems as part of ECMs to minimize energy use in groundwater management.
Conduct groundwater quality testing at defined locations and intervals to identify potential contamination and changes in groundwater quality.
Conduct soil quality testing at relevant locations to identify potential contamination associated with operational activities, spills, leaks, waste handling, or other potential pollution sources.
Review groundwater and soil testing results and initiate appropriate corrective or preventive actions where potential contamination or abnormal results are identified.

blocks.text:

Prepare SOPs for effluent treatment and pollution control.
Conduct regular wastewater quality tests to ensure effluent discharge complies with legal and environmental regulations.
Include groundwater protection measures in the CSR or Sustainability Report.
Maintain soil quality testing reports and associated environmental monitoring records.
Maintain records of identified groundwater/soil contamination risks and corrective or preventive actions, where applicable.
Maintain records of groundwater and soil monitoring results for periodic environmental review.

narrative.text:
Conduct monthly groundwater quality testing.
Maintain records of pollutant levels and corrective actions implemented.
Monitor soil quality at defined locations and intervals based on identified environmental risks and applicable monitoring requirements.
Review groundwater and soil monitoring trends periodically to identify potential pollution risks and improvement opportunities.

body.text:
Integrate water-saving devices such as low-flow fixtures, smart irrigation controllers, and water-efficient process equipment.
Utilize automated leak detection systems to promptly identify and address water losses.
Align the deployment of water conservation technologies with ECM objectives to maximize resource efficiency.
Implement and maintain suitable rainwater harvesting structures to capture rainwater and support groundwater recharge or other approved uses, where applicable.
Maintain suitable conveyance, filtration, collection, storage, or recharge arrangements for rainwater harvesting systems, as applicable to the installed system.
Inspect and clean rainwater harvesting structures periodically to maintain their effective operation.
Identify opportunities to enhance rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge based on site conditions, water availability, and water-risk assessment findings

blocks.text:
Maintain records of water-saving technology deployments.
Document system performance reviews and maintenance schedules.
Report annual water savings in the sustainability report.
Maintain records of rainwater harvesting structures, locations, inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and repair activities.
Maintain relevant technical assessments, completion certificates, photographs, and other supporting records for rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge initiatives, where applicable.
Where monitoring is performed, maintain records of groundwater levels and/or water quality associated with recharge activities.

narrative.text:
Conduct regular audits to evaluate the effectiveness of water conservation technologies.
Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to water usage efficiency.
Periodically review the effectiveness and condition of rainwater harvesting structures.
Monitor available data on rainwater harvesting, recharge, and water conservation performance and identify opportunities for improvement.

body.text:
Conduct periodic water-risk assessments to identify risks related to water availability, water consumption, groundwater dependence, water quality, wastewater discharge, and other relevant water-related issues.
Consider operational water requirements, water sources, local water availability, groundwater conditions, regulatory requirements, and potential environmental impacts when assessing water-related risks.
Identify significant water-related risks and establish appropriate mitigation or preventive measures.
Review water-related risks following significant changes in operations, water availability, regulatory requirements, or environmental conditions.

blocks.text:
Maintain records of completed water-risk assessments.
Document identified water-related risks, mitigation measures, responsible functions, and follow-up actions.

Monitor relevant wastewater-quality parameters based on applicable regulatory requirements and the characteristics of the wastewater.
Assess wastewater quality before discharge or reuse, as applicable.
Review wastewater monitoring results to identify deviations, environmental risks, and opportunities for improvement.
Initiate corrective and preventive actions where wastewater-quality results do not meet applicable requirements.

blocks.text:
Maintain wastewater-quality laboratory reports and monitoring records.
Maintain records of sampling dates, sampling locations, test parameters, results, and applicable standards or limits.
Maintain records of corrective and preventive actions arising from wastewater-quality monitoring.
Retain wastewater monitoring records for regulatory, environmental, and sustainability review.

Review all water conservation measures annually during sustainability audits.
Update SOPs, technologies, and practices based on advancements and audit findings.
Update this SOP when significant changes occur in operations, water-management technologies, regulatory requirements, or identified water-related risks.

To define and implement actions, technologies, and monitoring mechanisms aimed at reducing emissions of atmospheric pollutants, controlling environmental nuisances (noise, odor, vibration, light, and road congestion), and mitigating their impact on the environment. This SOP aims to ensure compliance with applicable environmental regulations and promote sustainable practices.

This SOP applies to all operational activities, equipment, and processes across the organization that have the potential to generate air or environmental pollutants, noise, odor, or other nuisances. It covers all facilities, production sites, warehouses, and associated infrastructure.

responsibilities: Implementation and maintenance of pollution control systems.
Oversight and adherence to environmental regulations, including reporting to relevant authorities.
Daily compliance with emission reduction practices.
Routine inspection and repair of emission control systems.
Verification of compliance with environmental standards.
Overall strategy and resource allocation.

body.text: 5.1 Prevention of Atmospheric Pollutants and Environmental Nuisances

Upgrade production processes to improve efficiency and reduce pollutant generation, such as low-emission burners and energy-efficient systems.
Install advanced pollution control equipment such as scrubbers, bag filters, and electrostatic precipitators (ESP Boilers) to capture and neutralize emissions at the source.
Transition from fire boilers to ESP boilers utilizing briquette and biomass fuels, significantly reducing carbon emissions and enhancing fuel efficiency.
Develop traffic management plans to minimize road congestion, including dedicated routes and optimized vehicle schedules.
Use shielded or directional lighting to prevent light pollution while maintaining operational safety.
Implement vibration damping measures such as vibration isolators for machinery and structural reinforcements.
Ensure noise barriers and other soundproofing measures are in place to mitigate noise at site boundaries.

rows.record: Installation and operational records of pollution control equipment
Actions taken and outcomes in Annual Reports or Sustainability Reports
Logs of compliance with local environmental regulations

blocks.text:
Maintain installation and operational records of pollution control equipment.
Include actions taken and outcomes in Annual Reports or Sustainability Reports.
Maintain logs of compliance with local environmental regulations.

Compliance with The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.
Adherence to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) Guidelines for emission standards.
Alignment with ISO 14001:2015 for Environmental Management Systems.
Observance of The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for environmental safeguards.

body.text:
Install dust collection and extraction systems, including cyclone separators, and wet scrubbers.
Utilize ESP boilers to enhance particulate matter control, ensuring compliance with stringent emission norms.
Use water sprinkler systems to suppress dust & gases in high-risk areas such as construction zones and bulk material handling.
Implement close system to control dusty operations, including vacuum systems for removal of fine particulate & gases.
Introduce vegetative cover or green belts in areas prone to dust generation to naturally reduce dust emissions.

narrative.text:
Conduct routine inspections of dust control measures and maintain calibration records for monitoring equipment.
Keep detailed logs of particulate matter reduction activities and their effectiveness.
Include dust control measures and monitoring results in quarterly environmental compliance reports.

Establish internal systems equipped with sensors and real-time monitoring tools to measure PM, NOx, SO2, VOC, and heavy metal levels.
Engage third-party services for ambient air quality analysis at predetermined intervals.
Conduct emissions dispersion modelling to assess potential impacts on the surrounding environment.

Prepare periodic air quality analysis reports and submit them to regulatory authorities as required.
Include air monitoring data, trends, and mitigation efforts in Annual and Sustainability Reports.
Display key air quality metrics on-site for transparency and public awareness.

sections.title: 5.4 VOC, SO2, NOx, and Heavy Metal Emission Mitigation

body.text:
Install scrubbers, adsorption systems, vapor recovery units, and airtight seals to capture and neutralize emissions.
Use catalytic or thermal oxidizers for VOC destruction in high-emission processes.
Optimize combustion processes to reduce NOx formation and introduce selective catalytic reduction (SCR) systems.
Implement advanced material handling systems to minimize heavy metal emissions during production.
Implement energy conservation measures (ECMs) such as optimizing steam usage and upgrading boilers to reduce SO2 emissions.
Leverage ESP boiler technology to improve efficiency in controlling SO2, NOx, and particulate emissions from biomass and briquette combustion.

blocks.text:
Maintain installation and operational records of all emission control technologies.
Regularly evaluate the performance of emission control systems using third-party audits.
Include emission mitigation data and impact assessments in Sustainability Reports.

body.text:
Conduct regular noise measurements at site boundaries using calibrated sound level meters.
Analyze noise data against permissible levels and prepare compliance reports.
Engage certified third-party agencies for periodic noise monitoring to validate internal findings.

Install acoustic enclosures, muffling controls, and noise barriers at high-noise equipment locations.
Develop a noise prevention maintenance plan to replace or repair faulty equipment that contributes to noise pollution.
Create a greenbelt around the facility to act as a natural sound barrier.
Train employees on noise mitigation practices and the importance of adhering to noise control measures.

Maintain maintenance logs, noise control system records, and employee training records.
Include noise monitoring data and mitigation strategies in CSR/Sustainability Reports.

Use isolated storage and advanced ventilation systems to contain and disperse odors.
Implement odor-neutralizing agents in storage and processing areas where odor generation is prevalent.
Employ activated carbon filters and biofilters in exhaust systems to remove odorous compounds.

Maintain records of odor control technology deployment and performance reviews.
Include odor mitigation efforts, results, and community feedback in Annual Reports.

Develop a structured LDAR program for identifying and repairing leaks in valves, pumps, compressors, and other equipment.
Use advanced monitoring tools such as leak detectors with alarm and gas analyzers.
Establish a database to track detected leaks, repair schedules, and verification tests.

Maintain detailed repair logs, program implementation records, and follow-up actions.
Conduct quarterly audits of LDAR effectiveness and submit findings in Sustainability Reports.

Establish an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) specific to air emission incidents, including procedures for accidental releases of hazardous pollutants.
Define clear roles and responsibilities during emergencies, including first responders, communication leads, and environmental officers.
Equip facilities with emergency kits, personal protective equipment (PPE), and spill containment tools.
Conduct regular emergency drills to test response readiness and improve procedures based on drill outcomes.
Maintain an emergency contact list, including local regulatory bodies and environmental response agencies.

blocks.text:
Annual review of pollution control measures and SOPs during environmental audits.
Update technologies and practices based on audit findings, advancements in environmental protection, and feedback from stakeholders.
Engage external consultants for expert recommendations on emerging pollutant control technologies.
Review the performance of ESP boilers regularly to ensure optimal emission control and compliance with environmental standards.

sops.title: MATERIAL SUSTAINABILITY AND HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCE MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES

blocks.text: To establish sustainable material management practices aimed at reducing material consumption, promoting the use of eco-friendly and recovered materials, and ensuring the safe handling, treatment, and disposal of hazardous substances. This SOP supports operational efficiency, environmental protection, and compliance with regulatory requirements.

This SOP applies to all operations, production processes, and supply chain activities where materials are consumed, handled, or disposed of within the organization. It includes guidelines for minimizing raw material usage, managing hazardous substances, and adopting sustainable practices.

responsibilities: Implementation of material sustainability and hazardous substance management practices.
Oversight of legal compliance and sustainability protocols.
Daily adherence to material efficiency and hazardous substance protocols.
Regular inspections and monitoring of hazardous material storage and disposal systems.
Identification and evaluation of process optimization opportunities for material consumption reduction, recovery, reuse, and waste minimization.
Monitoring of hazardous waste handling, treatment, disposal, and applicable environmental performance indicators.
Strategic planning and resource allocation.

sections.title: Process Optimization and Material Consumption Reduction

steps.heading: Process Optimization and Material Consumption Reduction

body.text: Operational Strategies:

Adopt process optimization technologies to reduce material consumption, such as lean manufacturing techniques and automation systems.
Improve product design and synthesis techniques to minimize raw material usage without compromising product quality.
Utilize advanced monitoring systems to track material usage and identify areas for reduction.
Evaluate production processes and operating parameters to identify opportunities to reduce raw material consumption while maintaining required product quality, yield, safety, and performance.
Optimize reaction conditions, process parameters, material yield, and production efficiency to minimize material losses and unnecessary consumption.
Evaluate opportunities to improve catalyst efficiency, catalyst recovery/reuse, chemical recovery, and recycling of suitable process inputs, wherever technically, operationally, and economically feasible.
Evaluate process modifications or technological improvements that can achieve the required product specifications with lower material input.
Where process changes are implemented for material efficiency, their technical feasibility, environmental benefits, product quality, and operational performance shall be evaluated and documented.

blocks.text:
Maintain records of process improvements and material consumption reports.
Include material efficiency metrics in sustainability audits.
Maintain records of significant process optimization initiatives undertaken for reduction of material consumption, improvement in yield, or reduction of material losses.
Where measurable data are available, record material consumption and relevant production/yield indicators before and after significant process improvements
Material Efficiency & Process Optimization Register

body.text:
Implement systems for the recovery of useful by-products, and chemical agents from production processes.
Adopt closed-loop recycling practices within operations to minimize raw material requirements.
Incorporate SO₂ recovery using a closed-loop system to enhance resource efficiency and reduce emissions.
Identify suitable process streams, by-products, recovered chemicals, and other materials that can be safely recovered and reused within operations, subject to technical feasibility, quality requirements, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Prioritize recovery and reuse of materials where this can reduce the requirement for virgin/raw materials or reduce waste generation.
Maintain appropriate controls to ensure that recovered materials are suitable for their intended reuse and do not adversely affect product quality, process safety, or environmental performance.

blocks.text:
Maintain logs of recovered materials and their subsequent use.
Report on material recovery efforts in sustainability reports.
Maintain records of material recovery, reuse, recycling, and closed-loop recovery initiatives, including relevant quantities where data are available.
Document significant changes or improvements to material recovery systems and their environmental/resource-efficiency benefits.
Material Recovery and Reuse Register.

body.text:
Use eco-friendly, biodegradable, or bio-based input materials to reduce environmental impact.
Replace non-renewable resources with sustainable alternatives where feasible.
Evaluate opportunities to substitute hazardous or higher-impact materials with less hazardous, lower-toxicity, eco-friendly, or bio-based alternatives where technically feasible.
Assess the potential environmental, health, safety, quality, and regulatory implications before introducing an alternative material.

sops.title: WASTE MINIMIZATION AND SUSTAINABLE DISPOSAL GUIDELINES

blocks.text: To establish waste minimization strategies and sustainable disposal practices aimed at reducing internal waste generation, enhancing waste segregation, and ensuring environmentally sound management of hazardous waste. This SOP supports efficient resource utilization, regulatory compliance, and environmental sustainability.

This SOP applies to all facilities, operational units, and waste management activities within the organization. It includes guidelines for waste reduction, sorting, recovery, mapping of waste streams, and proper disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste.

responsibilities: Implementation of waste reduction and disposal strategies.
Oversight of waste management compliance and sustainability initiatives.
Daily adherence to waste segregation and minimization practices.
Supervision of waste handling equipment and infrastructure.

rows.role: Concerned Department Heads / Waste Generating Departments
responsibilities: Identification of waste generation points, implementation of source segregation and identification of opportunities for reuse, recovery or repurposing.
Maintenance of waste inventories, waste-stream mapping, manifest tracking, review of disposal routes and monitoring of compliance with applicable requirements.
Strategic planning and resource allocation.
Ensure implementation of waste minimization, segregation, recovery and disposal requirements within their respective areas.

blocks.text: Waste Prevention and Resource Recovery

substeps.text: Promote material reuse by replacing disposable items with reusable alternatives wherever feasible.
Identify opportunities to prevent or reduce waste generation at the source through improved process practices, efficient material utilization and operational controls.
Prioritize waste prevention and reduction before recovery, treatment or final disposal, wherever technically feasible and legally permissible.
Evaluate process activities that generate significant quantities of waste and identify opportunities to reduce material losses and avoid unnecessary waste generation.
Implement recovery systems to reclaim valuable materials from production by-products.
Identify suitable process by-products, residues and internally generated materials for recovery, recycling or reuse within operations, where technically feasible and approved.
Promote recovery of useful materials before sending waste for final disposal.
Where internal recovery or reuse is not feasible, suitable authorized recovery or recycling routes shall be evaluated before disposal.
Utilize recovered waste materials, such as spent lime sludge, sulphur sludge, and spent catalyst, in compliance with approved recycling or disposal practices.
Repurpose obsolete equipment and materials within operations to reduce waste generation.
Where technically and operationally feasible, identify suitable materials and equipment that can be repurposed for another approved use rather than being discarded.
Reuse, recovery or repurposing shall be carried out without compromising product quality, process safety, environmental requirements or applicable legal requirements.
Contaminated materials and chemical packaging shall not be reused unless such reuse is specifically permitted by applicable safety, SDS and regulatory requirements.
Implement internal waste sorting systems categorized into paper, glass, metals, plastics, organic waste, and hazardous waste.
Segregate waste at the point of generation according to its applicable waste stream before transfer to storage, treatment, recovery, recycling or disposal.
Hazardous and non-hazardous waste shall be kept segregated to prevent cross-contamination, unsafe mixing and inappropriate disposal.
Waste shall be identified according to its nature, physical form, hazard characteristics and applicable treatment/disposal requirements.
Incompatible hazardous waste streams shall not be mixed where such mixing could create a safety, environmental or treatment risk.
Utilize color-coded bins and clear labelling to facilitate proper waste segregation.
Ensure proper labelling of hazardous waste containers as per Form No-8 and maintain compliance with GPCB regulations.
Waste containers shall be suitable for the waste characteristics and maintained in designated storage areas to prevent leakage, spillage or uncontrolled release.
Hazardous chemical residues and contaminated packaging shall be handled and stored with reference to the applicable Safety Data Sheet (SDS) and approved waste-management requirements.
Adopt specialized disposal methods for each waste category, such as recycling, composting, or incineration for hazardous waste.
Waste shall be directed to an appropriate recycling, recovery, treatment or disposal route based on its characteristics and applicable regulatory requirements.
Where recovery or recycling is technically feasible and legally permissible, such routes shall be considered before final disposal.
Hazardous waste shall be transferred only through approved and authorized waste-management arrangements.
Disposal methods shall be selected to prevent adverse impacts on human health and the environment.
Maintain logs of waste sorted and quantities directed to various disposal methods.
Include waste segregation data in environmental compliance reports.
Maintain records of waste quantities by waste stream and the corresponding recovery, recycling, treatment or disposal route, as applicable.
Records shall be reviewed periodically to identify abnormal increases in waste generation and opportunities for improved segregation or recovery.
Identify significant waste-generation points across operational areas and document the applicable waste streams generated from each source.
Identify the responsible department/area associated with each waste stream to support proper segregation, handling and accountability.
Waste characteristics, physical form, storage requirements and applicable treatment/recovery/disposal route shall be identified, where applicable.
Develop comprehensive waste stream maps to track waste flow from generation to final disposal.
Identify critical control points to optimize waste reduction and recovery efforts.
Conduct regular audits to assess the effectiveness of waste stream management.
Track hazardous waste streams using the internal and external manifest system for regulatory compliance and traceability.

Waste-flow tracking shall cover, as applicable, the movement from generation → segregation → internal storage/handling → transportation → treatment/recovery/recycling → final disposal or other approved destination.
Waste-flow information shall be reviewed to identify opportunities for waste prevention, recovery, recycling and resource efficiency.
Significant changes in processes, raw materials, waste generation points or disposal/recovery arrangements shall be considered when updating waste-flow information.

substeps.text: Restrict transboundary movement of hazardous waste unless it aligns with environmentally sound management practices.
Hazardous waste shall be managed through authorized and environmentally sound treatment, recovery, recycling or disposal routes.
Hazardous waste shall not be transferred to unauthorized persons, facilities or disposal routes.

Where transboundary movement of hazardous waste is applicable, such movement shall be prohibited or restricted unless all applicable legal requirements, approvals and environmentally sound management conditions are satisfied.

blocks.text: To establish best practices for efficient product use, safe storage, and maintenance to extend product life, reduce environmental impact, and minimize hazardous emissions. This SOP ensures compliance with sustainability objectives while enhancing product safety and performance.

This SOP applies to all chemical and durable products manufactured, stored, and distributed by the company. It includes guidelines on product efficiency, optimized design, safe handling, storage, labelling, and reduction of toxic discharges.

blocks.text: Efficient Product Use, Storage, and Maintenance

body.text:
Develop and maintain appropriate product guidelines for customers/users to support efficient and intended use of products and, where applicable, extend the useful life of durable products.
Provide relevant instructions on recommended product use, handling and application practices to minimize unnecessary resource consumption, product loss and wastage while maintaining product effectiveness.
For chemical products, provide applicable Safety Data Sheets (SDS), product labels and technical information covering safe handling, application and storage requirements.
Ensure that product-use information supports appropriate application and handling practices to minimize leakages or unintended release of harmful substances.
Ensure proper storage conditions to prevent degradation, leakages, and environmental contamination.

Specify appropriate storage conditions, including temperature, ventilation, container closure and protection from incompatible substances, as applicable to the product.
Ensure that product containers are maintained in suitable condition and kept properly closed to prevent leakage, deterioration or uncontrolled release.
Provide precautionary information for preventing product release to drains, soil or other environmental receptors, where applicable.
Review product storage and handling information periodically and update it when product characteristics, regulatory requirements or safety information change.

Provide relevant product-use and safety information through applicable product labels, SDS, technical documents or other approved customer communication channels.
Ensure that information provided to customers/users is consistent with the approved product specification, SDS and applicable regulatory requirements.
Maintain records demonstrating the provision and communication of applicable product-use, storage and handling information.

steps.heading: Product Use, Storage and Handling Information Register

body.text:

The register may include product name, intended use/application, recommended handling/use information, storage conditions, leakage/release prevention measures, applicable SDS/label reference and customer/user information provided.
Review the register periodically and update it following relevant product, process, regulatory or safety changes.

steps.heading: Chemical Product Efficiency and Sustainable Design

body.text: Product Efficiency and Application Optimization:

Evaluate opportunities during product development, modification or improvement to enhance chemical product efficiency and achieve the intended performance with reduced dosage, quantity or application frequency, where technically feasible.
Consider product characteristics, formulation, concentration, reaction/application efficiency and performance requirements that may enable reduced material consumption during intended use.
Where an improved product demonstrates equivalent or improved performance at a lower dosage, quantity or application frequency compared with a reference or existing product, document the technical evaluation and comparison.
Ensure that product efficiency improvements do not compromise product quality, safety, regulatory compliance or intended performance.
Dosage and Application Efficiency Evaluation:

Conduct appropriate technical trials, product comparison studies or performance evaluations, where applicable, to determine whether product improvements can reduce dosage, quantity or frequency of use.
Document the basis for any claimed reduction, including the reference product/condition, improved product characteristic, dosage or application requirement and corresponding performance results.
Use documented technical evidence to support communication of product efficiency benefits to relevant customers/users, where applicable.

Evaluate product formulation and design options that may reduce toxic discharges, harmful residues or environmental releases during the intended use of chemical products, where technically feasible.
Develop less hazardous chemical alternatives that reduce harmful emissions.
Utilize less hazardous additives to ensure safe environmental degradation.
Eliminate or substitute hazardous substances in formulations to comply with global safety standards.
Consider product composition, hazardous substance content and potential environmental impacts when evaluating product improvements or alternative formulations.

steps.heading: Hazardous Substance Substitution and Product Improvement

body.text:
Evaluate the substitution or reduction of hazardous substances with less hazardous or less toxic alternatives, where technically feasible and consistent with product performance and regulatory requirements.
Where a product modification demonstrates reduced toxic discharge potential or reduced environmental impact compared with an existing/reference product, document the technical basis and comparative assessment.
Consider available product safety, environmental and technical information during product development and improvement activities.

Where applicable, assess relevant environmental characteristics of improved chemical products, including potential toxic discharges, harmful residues, emissions or environmental releases.
Use appropriate technical studies, product comparison assessments, environmental assessments or other documented evidence to substantiate environmental improvements.
Ensure that environmental improvements do not adversely affect product quality, safety, intended performance or applicable regulatory requirements.

The register should include the product, environmental concern, existing product characteristic, design/formulation improvement, expected environmental benefit, supporting technical evidence and applicable safety/regulatory review.

Include relevant recommended-use, handling, storage, disposal and emergency response information, as applicable to the product.
Clearly indicate applicable storage conditions, temperature requirements, container/handling precautions and expiration or retest details, where relevant, to prevent misuse or degradation.
Ensure product labels provide information consistent with the applicable SDS and approved product information.

Use digital logs to track compliance with safety measures and environmental regulations.
Where applicable, maintain digital records of product information, SDS, technical documents, product-use information and product improvement records to support traceability.

sops.title: COMPLIANCE, ETHICS, AND RISK ASSESSMENT GUIDELINES

blocks.text: To establish a structured approach for conducting audits, risk assessments, and compliance reviews to prevent corruption, unethical practices, and other business risks. This SOP ensures adherence to legal, financial, ethical, and social responsibility standards while protecting corporate integrity.

This SOP applies to all internal operational, financial, HR, and regulatory compliance activities at Transpek Industry Ltd. It includes guidelines for internal audits, external reviews, anti-corruption measures, social issue assessments, and ethical risk mitigation.

responsibilities: Conduct audits, internal control reviews, and risk assessments.
Ensure financial transparency, prevent fraud, and manage internal controls.
Promote ethical hiring, workplace conduct, and social responsibility.
Ensure adherence to regulatory policies and ethical governance.

body.text:
Conduct periodic internal audits and control assessments covering relevant financial, ethical, anti-corruption, information security, operational, and compliance controls based on identified risks and the approved audit scope.
Define the scope, assessment criteria, applicable departments/functions, and period covered for each audit or control assessment.
Regular internal audits covering financial transactions, HR policies, workplace ethics, and operational compliance.
Include anti-corruption and information security controls in internal assessments, as applicable.

Assign the responsible person or function for planning, conducting, reviewing, and following up each audit or control assessment.
The accountable function shall ensure that audit findings are documented, corrective actions are assigned, and follow-up is completed.
Audit & Compliance Teams – Conduct audits, internal control reviews, and risk assessments.
Relevant functional heads shall provide necessary information, support the assessment, and implement assigned corrective actions.

Review previous audit reports, assessment results, identified non-conformities, and corrective actions to determine whether previously identified control weaknesses have been addressed.
Evaluate the effectiveness of existing ethical, anti-corruption, and information security controls through review of previous findings, current assessment results, and implementation of corrective actions.
Retrospective analysis of past audit reports to assess system improvements.

Document audit and assessment findings and identify appropriate corrective actions for identified gaps or control weaknesses.
Assign responsible persons and target completion dates for corrective actions, where applicable.
Verify the implementation and effectiveness of corrective actions through follow-up review or subsequent assessment.
Track corrective actions until completion.

blocks.text:
Maintain audit reports, corrective action records, and compliance tracking logs.
Maintain defined audit scope, assessment checklists, supporting evidence, findings, responsible persons, corrective actions, follow-up verification, and management review records.
Include findings and improvements in annual compliance reports.

Ensure transparency and accountability in financial transactions, operational decision-making, and policy enforcement.
Conduct internal audits and governance reviews to prevent financial misconduct, conflicts of interest, and unethical practices.
Assess corruption and ethical risks associated with relevant business activities and third-party interactions.
Implement governance training programs to educate employees on corporate integrity, ethical decision-making, and compliance obligations.

body.text:
Maintain governance audit reports, financial compliance records, and risk management assessments.
Ensure adherence to corporate governance principles, ethical business conduct policies, and regulatory requirements.
Maintain documented evidence of identified governance risks, assessments performed, corrective actions, and follow-up activities.

blocks.text: Workplace Ethics and Labor Rights:

Assess compliance with labor laws, workplace diversity, and fair treatment policies.
Monitor working conditions, wages, and employee welfare.
Identify and mitigate risks related to discrimination, harassment, and forced labor.
Community and Environmental Impact:

Evaluate company policies on environmental sustainability and social responsibility.
Monitor community grievances related to corporate operations.
Engage with local stakeholders to address social and environmental concerns.

Maintain records of workplace audits, social risk assessments, and stakeholder engagement reports.
Include social responsibility performance in sustainability reports.

sections.title: Third-Party Ethical Due Diligence and Compliance Assessment

steps.heading: Third-Party Risk Screening and Due Diligence

body.text:
Identify third parties that may create ethical, corruption, compliance, or information security risks, including suppliers, vendors, consultants, agents, brokers, distributors, contractors, customs brokers, sales representatives, and other business intermediaries, as applicable.
Conduct appropriate due diligence before onboarding or engaging relevant third parties, based on the nature of the business relationship and associated risks.
Review available information relating to the third party’s business activities, ownership or management, ethical practices, regulatory compliance, and potential conflicts of interest, as applicable.
Obtain and review relevant declarations, questionnaires, compliance commitments, or supporting documents where required.
Document the due diligence performed and the outcome of the assessment.

Use Supplier Self-Assessments, Supplier On-Site ESG Audits, Internal Assessments, and other applicable assessment mechanisms to evaluate third-party compliance and ethical risks.
Assess relevant third parties against applicable anti-corruption, ethical conduct, information security, and compliance requirements.
Review identified gaps, non-conformities, observations, and risks arising from third-party assessments.
Record appropriate corrective actions and follow-up requirements for identified gaps.
Consider assessment results when reviewing the continuation or improvement of the business relationship, as applicable.

sections.title: Enhanced Review for Higher-Risk Third Parties

blocks.text:
Where a third party is identified as having higher ethical, corruption, compliance, or information security risk, additional review or supporting information may be requested based on the nature and risk of the relationship.
The extent of additional due diligence shall be determined based on the identified risk and business relationship.
Document the additional review and its outcome where performed.

Review the results of third-party due diligence and assessments before approval or continuation of the relevant business relationship, as applicable.
Communicate identified requirements or corrective actions to the concerned third party or responsible internal function.
Track corrective actions arising from supplier or third-party assessments until closure or appropriate resolution.
Conduct follow-up assessment or verification where required based on the identified risk or previous findings.

Maintain records of third-party due diligence, Supplier Self-Assessments, Supplier On-Site ESG Audits, internal assessment results, supporting documents, identified risks, corrective actions, and follow-up verification.
Maintain records in accordance with the Company's applicable document and records management requirements.

narrative.text:
Establish confidential whistleblower mechanisms for reporting unethical activities.
Ensure all reports are reviewed by an independent ethics committee.
Investigate allegations thoroughly and implement corrective actions.
Protect employees from retaliation when reporting unethical behaviour.

blocks.text:
Conduct annual reviews of compliance programs and audit procedures.
Update SOPs based on regulatory changes and audit findings.
Monitor new trends in corporate governance, and social responsibility.

sops.title: DATA PRIVACY AND RECORDS MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES

blocks.text: To establish best practices for data retention, protection, and stakeholder consent management to ensure compliance with privacy regulations, confidentiality standards, and corporate governance policies.

This SOP applies to all third-party, customer, and internal confidential data collected, stored, processed, and retained by the company. It includes data handling procedures, access control measures, and retention policies to prevent unauthorized disclosure and ensure compliance.

responsibilities: Conduct audits, internal control reviews, and risk assessments.
Ensure financial transparency, prevent fraud, and manage internal controls.
Promote ethical hiring, workplace conduct, and social responsibility.
Ensure adherence to regulatory policies and ethical governance.

body.text: Security Measures for Data Protection:

Implement access control mechanisms to restrict unauthorized physical or digital access to third-party or customer data.
Use encryption and multi-factor authentication (MFA) for sensitive data protection.
Monitor and log all access attempts to detect and prevent unauthorized data breaches.
Establish data segregation protocols to ensure minimal data exposure between departments.

blocks.text:
Maintain access logs and security compliance reports.
Conduct regular penetration testing and security audits.
Maintain records of identified information-security risks, control measures, assessment findings and corrective actions, as applicable.

body.text:
Provide clear and transparent information to customers, clients, employees and other relevant stakeholders regarding the collection, processing, sharing and retention of their personal or confidential information.
Communicate the relevant purpose and nature of information collected before or at the time of collection, as applicable.
Inform stakeholders, where applicable, about the categories or types of information collected and the intended use of such information.
Inform stakeholders where personal or confidential information may be shared with authorized third parties or service providers, in accordance with applicable requirements.
Provide information regarding applicable data retention requirements or periods, where required.

Ensure clear and transparent communication with stakeholders regarding the collection, processing, and retention of their data.
Provide stakeholders with an explicit opt-in mechanism before collecting personal or confidential data.
Disclose data-sharing policies to inform stakeholders about third-party data processing agreements.
Obtain and document stakeholder consent where consent is the applicable legal or operational basis for collecting, processing or sharing personal information.
Allow stakeholders to request modifications or deletions of their stored data in compliance with data privacy laws.

blocks.text:
Maintain records of consent agreements and privacy policy updates.
Store communication logs related to data privacy disclosures.
Maintain records demonstrating the information provided to stakeholders regarding data collection, processing, sharing and retention, where applicable.
Maintain records of requests received from stakeholders and actions taken in response, where applicable.

body.text:
Establish a structured records retention schedule specifying the duration for storing third-party, customer, and internal data.
Classify records based on type (e.g., financial, legal, operational, personal data) and define retention timelines for each category.
Automate record retention policies through digital management systems to ensure compliance.
Data Retention Schedule:

blocks.text:
Maintain records retention logs and periodic compliance audits.
Ensure retention policies align with legal and regulatory requirements.

narrative.text:
Establish a defined process for identifying and reporting suspected information-security breaches, unauthorized disclosures, data leaks, phishing attempts, malware incidents and other cybersecurity events.
Employees and relevant personnel shall promptly report suspected information-security incidents through the designated reporting channel.
The Information Security Officer or designated responsible person shall record and assess reported incidents to determine the nature and potential impact of the breach.

body.text:
Develop an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) for data breaches, unauthorized disclosures, and cyber threats.
Define roles and responsibilities for IT security, legal, and compliance teams in the event of a data breach.
Investigate the reported breach to determine its cause, affected information, affected systems and potential impact.
Take appropriate containment measures to limit unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, loss or further spread of confidential information.
Implement recovery measures appropriate to the nature and severity of the incident.

Notify affected stakeholders and regulatory authorities in accordance with applicable data protection laws.
Where a breach affects customers, employees, suppliers or other stakeholders, provide appropriate communication regarding the incident and relevant protective or corrective measures, where required.
Restrict further disclosure of confidential information and implement appropriate measures to protect affected information.

blocks.text:
Conduct root cause analysis and corrective actions to prevent future incidents.
Document the incident, investigation findings, containment measures, corrective actions and closure status.
Review existing information-security controls following significant incidents and strengthen controls where gaps or weaknesses are identified.
Track corrective actions until completion and verify effectiveness where appropriate.

Maintain information-security incident reports, investigation records, breach assessment records, communication records, corrective-action records and closure evidence, as applicable.
Maintain records of information-security assessments and reviews used to evaluate the effectiveness of security controls.
Ensure information-security records are protected against unauthorized access, alteration or disclosure.

Conduct annual reviews of data retention schedules, security controls, and consent management policies.
Review information-security incident trends, stakeholder consent practices, data-processing arrangements and identified control weaknesses to identify opportunities for improvement.
Update SOPs based on regulatory changes and cybersecurity trends.
Monitor evolving global data protection laws to ensure proactive compliance.
Implement improvements arising from incident investigations, security assessments, audits and corrective actions.

sops.title: SUSTAINABLE PROCUREMENT AND ETHICAL SOURCING GUIDELINES

blocks.text: To establish a structured approach for integrating sustainability objectives into procurement processes and buyer performance evaluations. This SOP ensures that ethical sourcing, environmental responsibility, and supplier sustainability are key factors in procurement decision-making.

This SOP applies to all procurement activities, supplier assessments, and buyer performance evaluations at Transpek Industry Ltd. It includes guidelines for sustainable procurement strategies, ethical sourcing, and the integration of sustainability metrics into buyer performance reviews.

responsibilities: Implement sustainable procurement strategies and supplier assessments.
Monitor financial integrity and ethical compliance in procurement.
Evaluate procurement personnel based on sustainability criteria.
Ensure supplier adherence to environmental and ethical standards.

blocks.text:
Preference for suppliers with strong environmental, social, and governance (ESG) policies.
Adoption of sustainable raw materials and packaging by vendors.
Evaluation of suppliers based on carbon footprint, water conservation, and waste management.
Encouraging procurement from local and ethically certified sources.

rows.record: Supplier sustainability assessment reports
Supplier contracts and agreements including sustainability metrics

sections.title: Integration of Sustainability in Buyer Performance

blocks.text:
Assess buyers based on their ability to source from sustainable suppliers.
Include supplier sustainability performance as a defined criterion in the performance evaluation of buyers responsible for supplier selection, management, and interaction.
Evaluate buyers, as applicable, on their implementation of supplier sustainability assessment, monitoring, corrective-action follow-up, and engagement activities
Include sustainability KPIs in buyer performance evaluations, such as:
Percentage of applicable suppliers assessed against defined sustainability criteria.
Percentage of applicable suppliers meeting required sustainability/compliance criteria.
Completion of supplier sustainability assessments and follow-up actions within defined timelines.
Reduction in procurement-related environmental impact.
Compliance with fair labor and ethical trade standards.
Buyers must demonstrate efforts in promoting sustainable supply chain initiatives.
The sustainability-related performance of buyers shall be reviewed as part of the applicable buyer performance appraisal process

Corrective actions for non-compliance with sustainable procurement standards
Evidence of supplier sustainability assessments, supplier audit results, corrective-action follow-up, and buyer performance evaluation records used to assess sustainability-related objectives

blocks.text:

Require transparency in supply chain practices to prevent human rights violations.
Ensure compliance with hazardous substance regulations and responsible material sourcing.

Periodic supplier audits and compliance records

blocks.text:
Implement digital tracking systems for monitoring supplier sustainability performance.
Utilize procurement dashboards to analyze real-time sustainability metrics.

Periodic sustainability reports for internal and external stakeholders

Conduct annual reviews of sustainable procurement strategies and buyer performance evaluations.
Update SOPs based on audit findings, regulatory changes, and emerging sustainability trends.
Engage with external sustainability experts to enhance ethical sourcing initiatives.
Monitor buyer compliance with sustainability KPIs and implement continuous training programs.
